title: A full grid reads as a strong case
text: Separate elements and each one needs its own proof. Build the chart and the easy move is to treat a full grid as a strong case. Every box has an entry, so every element must be covered. title: The anchor — one cited, one gapped
text: Chart works element by element. For every element it finds the passage that could support it and pin sites the exact page and line. Watch two elements from the same claim. A locking mechanism turns up a citation straight to the product manual, page 12. A temperature sensor turns up nothing in the same manual, no citation exists to put in that cell. title: Filled ≠ proven, gap ≠ failed
text: Mechanism cell reads supported manual page 12 and the temperature sensor cell reads no citation found a gap, flagged on purpose. A filled cell doesn't decide the case. A citation can be weak or cover only part of the element. And a gap doesn't decide it either. It isn't proof the element fails, only proof no evidence has turned up yet. title: Carry-out
text: A claim chart isn't a full grid, it's a pin site for what's supported and a flag element by element for what's missing.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn. Here's the prompt, read it with me. Paste in the claim language element by element along with the accused product's documentation. Then ask for each element, find the exact passage that supports it, site it, and flag any element with no citation as a gap. Don't guess to fill it in. Lay them in for bare.
